anomaly_def.Name: Transaction Lock Contention Anomaly + Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly + Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Transaction Lock Contention Anomaly : Concurrent transactions request incompatible locks on the same data or metadata resources, creating long blocking chains or deadlocks that stall progress until a waiter times out or the engine aborts a victim. 
Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly : Critical engine parameters (memory, checkpoint cadence, parallelism, etc.) are mis-tuned for the hardware or workload, causing subsystem behavior that is sub-optimal even though the underlying resources are not yet exhausted. 
Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly : The physical storage layer becomes a hard bottleneck as sustained reads or writes exceed the throughput, IOPS, or latency capacity of the devices that host data, temp, or log files.

When all three root causes manifest together, the database experiences a reinforcing storm of symptoms: lock wait queues grow while overall I/O wait events dominate session profiles; transactions linger in locked states because every page or row access incurs inflated disk latency; checkpoint or log-flush surges—driven by mis-sized buffers or too-aggressive durability settings—collide with an already saturated storage subsystem, further stretching lock hold times. Users observe erratic response times, frequent deadlock victim errors, sporadic application timeouts, and sharp drops in throughput even though CPU may appear lightly loaded. Monitoring shows simultaneous spikes in lock waits, log write waits, buffer-I/O stalls, and background writer or checkpoint activity, making it difficult to attribute the slowdown to any single layer.

Causal chain: sub-optimal configuration (e.g., undersized buffer pool, overly frequent checkpoints, small log files, or excessive parallel workers) forces the engine to issue more physical I/O and to flush dirty pages or logs more often. The increased I/O demand pushes the storage system past its throughput limit, inflating read/write latencies. Longer I/O times lengthen transaction execution and commit phases, extending the duration that locks are held. Prolonged lock ownership heightens the probability of conflicting lock requests, spawning longer blocking chains and deadlocks. In turn, the growing population of waiting sessions can exhaust connection and memory quotas already constrained by poor configuration, provoking further swapping, emergency checkpoints, or log stalls that deepen the storage overload. The three anomalies thus amplify one another, creating a feedback loop that degrades both concurrency control and physical I/O, culminating in severe throughput collapse for transactional workloads.

entry.official_definition: Specifies the timeout in seconds for attempts to acquire metadata locks.
entry.trigger_condition: A statement waits longer than lock_wait_timeout while attempting to acquire a metadata lock.
entry.workload_impact: The metadata lock acquisition fails and the statement does not proceed.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL server system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when a statement cannot obtain the required lock within the configured waiting window because another transaction or metadata operation is holding an incompatible lock.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect blocking sessions, reduce conflicting transaction overlap, shorten transaction lifetime, and review lock scheduling and schema-change timing.
